note: B lacks the remittance transfer amendments to the authority and purpose text that A has taken (and has a different OMB number).
B has the 2010-2011 fee limits ($25/$35, no smaller card issuer rule) while A has the later $8/$32/$43 safe harbors, smaller card issuer provision and inflation adjustments.
A lacks the later amendments B has taken (subpart B cross-references for small business data collection and the 5(a)(4) information retention), with A history ending 2011.
A limits the section to Federal Reserve member banks and related entities while B applies it to any person not excluded by the Consumer Financial Protection Act; the rule is otherwise the same.
B lacks the identity theft definition that A has, plus minor FCRA abbreviation and numbering differences.

B has the 2010 ability-to-pay text requiring independent ability for all applicants, while A has the 2013 amendment allowing reasonable expectation of access to income and dropping the credit line increase paragraph (b)(2)(i) split.
B lacks the LIBOR transition provisions in (f)(3) and (h)(3) that A has taken.
A lacks the RESPA/TILA integrated-disclosure preemption sentence and updated cross-reference (N.60 instead of N.5a) that B has taken.
B is pre-Dodd-Frank (still lists Office of Thrift Supervision, two-year limitation, FTC enforcement without the CFPB), while A has the CFPB, five-year limitations period and removes OTS.
